body.statement: Fix \(q<1/4\) and the amplitudes in \(\mathrm{def:markov\mbox{-}witness}\). For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), the bounded Markov law \(W_\ell\) lies in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(1,1,1,q,B,\theta\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\), but its arm means depend on \(A_{i,j-1}\), so it is not generated by the exogenous unit and time factors in Dwivedi et al.'s published equation (4) on page 2383. Conversely, their published Assumption 6 on page 2397 and Theorem 4.1 on page 2398 contain the bounded Lipschitz nonlinear-factor law generated by \(f^{\mathrm D}_0\), \(f^{\mathrm D}_1\), \(u^{\mathrm D}\), and \(v^{\mathrm D}\), for which \(\operatorname{rank}(M^{\mathrm D})=\min(n,m)\) almost surely; this law is excluded by \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\) for fixed \(r\). Thus their unit-by-time nearest-neighbor bound in published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 and the normalized maximum-row IPW-SVD frontier are non-representable in either direction.
body.justification: This gives the exact model-theoretic separation from the closest adaptive pooled unit-by-time factor result.
body.gap: Dwivedi et al., published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389, control a nearest-neighbor unit-by-time arm-mean error under the factor structure in equation (4) on page 2383, not a row-subspace loss under treatment-path-dependent arm means.
body.consumer: Referees can distinguish the row-factor target and predictable-mask domain from published adaptive counterfactual imputation.
